title: A Proto-Agent can perform no actions until it transforms into either a Prime Agent or an Executor Agent
content:
A.2.2.5.2 states the constraint plainly: a Proto-Agent "has not yet adopted any specialized role. Since a Proto-Agent cannot perform actions in the Sky Ecosystem, it must first transform into either a Prime Agent or Executor Agent to gain functionality."

The Transformation Primitive's actual input is minimal — the desired Agent Type, with 'Prime Agent' specified for the Prime path (A.2.2.5.2.1.1.1) — but the validation attached to it is not. A.2.2.5.2.1.1.2 has Core GovOps re-review everything the Founder built under Founder Access for specification quality and Alignment, and confirm that all six required Primitives are Activated. Transformation is therefore the **audit checkpoint** of Agent formation, not merely a type declaration.

Once Invoked, the Instance Status is `Completed` (A.2.2.5.2.1.1.3) and "no further management process is needed post-deployment" (A.2.2.5.2.1.2.1). Combined with the prohibition on deactivating Genesis Primitives, the choice between Prime and Executor is made once, under one review, and is not revisited through this mechanism.

The consequence is that Sky's two-sided Agent architecture — Primes holding strategy, Executors holding operations — is enforced at the moment of birth rather than by ongoing classification. An Agent cannot drift between roles or occupy both.
description: Role selection is a compulsory one-time gate: transformation is what confers functionality, and the resulting Instance is `Completed` and never revisited.
